issues.description: The problem statement contains conflicting specifications for the collection type used to store animals in Farm: the UML shows animals: List<Animal> while the Part 3 textual instructions explicitly require a Set implemented using a HashSet. The provided solution implements animals as a List/ArrayList. This mismatch (UML vs. textual requirement vs. solution) can confuse students about which collection type to use and affects behavior (uniqueness/duplicates) and the required constructor initialization.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) update the problem statement UML to show animals: Set<Animal> (and mention HashSet in the UML or notes) and update the solution/template to initialize a HashSet, or (B) keep the UML List and change the textual instructions to request a List/ArrayList and remove the HashSet requirement. Ensure the template Farm constructor and field match the chosen collection type and provide a getter/setter consistent with that type.

issues.description: The problem statement requires the Farm's collection of animals to be implemented as a Set (specifically a HashSet) to enforce uniqueness, while the solution implements the animals attribute as a List (ArrayList). This mismatch in the collection type identifier (Set/HashSet vs List/ArrayList) creates conceptual mapping confusion: students following the instructions will expect Set semantics (no duplicates) and a HashSet initialization, but the provided solution and template code use List semantics, which may allow duplicates and different API usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts. Either update the solution and template to use a Set<Animal> and initialize it with a new HashSet<>() in the no-argument constructor, and adjust any code that relies on List-specific behavior; or modify the problem statement to accept List<Animal> (ArrayList) and remove the HashSet requirement. Prefer aligning solution and template with the explicit problem instruction to use Set/HashSet.
